{"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","hash":"0c337c5cd362499b140f994d72f07b2be1b1e283166b4625083169ae749184c1","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_01NCTjYwYejme6QzBQgFaJae","content":"Launching skill: tdd"},{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01JSVK11Epo1QBhLqpcTtQxP","type":"tool_result","content":"# Kenyon Model UN Recaps\n\nA content system where the Kenyon Model UN club's officers publish recaps of the club's conference trips for the Kenyon community.\n\n## Content\n\n**Trip**:\nOne conference journey the club made, such as the Chicago conference. A Trip carries its own required Summary of what the trip was, and groups the Recaps written about it. A Trip appears on the Public site only once it has at least one Published Recap, and it can be deleted only while it has no Recaps.\n_Avoid_: Event, conference (as the record's name)\n\n**Summary**:\nAn Admin-written overview on a Trip: the conference, where it was, and what happened overall. Readers see it at the top of the Trip's page.\n_Avoid_: Description, intro\n\n**Recap**:\nOne club member's personal account of exactly one Trip. A Recap has a title, a Slug, a Markdown body with optional Images, a Byline, an Owner, and records of when it was created, last edited, and Published. It is written by an Editor, or entered by an Admin for a Contributor. Recaps are individual anecdotes, while the Trip's Summary says what the trip was. A Trip can have several Recaps.\n_Avoid_: Post, blog, article\n\n**Slug**:\nThe short, URL-safe name that identifies a Trip, Recap, or Page in the public site's addresses, such as `2026-chicago` or `chicago-food-crawl`. A Trip's Slug is unique among Trips, a Recap's within its Trip, and a Page's among Pages. A Page cannot take a Slug the site already uses, such as `trips` or `images`.\n_Avoid_: Permalink, path, handle\n\n**Byline**:\nThe writer's name and class year shown on a Recap, such as \"by Jane Doe '27\". Both parts are required. An Editor's or Admin's Byline comes from their Account, and an Admin types a Contributor's Byline by hand. The Byline is separate from the Recap's Owner.\n_Avoid_: Author (an Admin who typed a Recap in is not its writer)\n\n**Owner**:\nThe Account a Recap or Page belongs to: the Editor who wrote it, or the Admin who created it or entered it for a Contributor. \"Their own Recap\" means a Recap they Own.\n_Avoid_: Author, creator\n\n**Image**:\nA photo uploaded to a Recap and placed inline in its body, always with alt text. Images belong to Recaps only. Recaps show only uploaded Images, never ones hosted elsewhere.\n_Avoid_: Media, attachment, embed\n\n**Page**:\nStanding content about the club that is not tied to a Trip, such as \"About the club\" or \"Officers and contact\". A Page has a title, a Slug, a text-only Markdown body, a Draft or Published status, an Owner, and records of when it was created and last edited. Only Admins create, edit, or delete Pages.\n_Avoid_: Static page, post\n\n**Body**:\nThe Markdown text of a Recap or Page. A Body never links to outside sites or shows images hosted elsewhere.\n_Avoid_: Content, text (for this field)\n\n**Navigation bar**:\nThe list of links across the top of the public site: a Home link first, then the Published Pages in the order Admins set.\n_Avoid_: Menu, header links\n\n## Publishing\n\n**Public site**:\nThe static website the Kenyon community reads: Trips that have a Published Recap, their Published Recaps, the Published Pages, and the Navigation bar. Deploy produces it. Nothing else reaches it.\n_Avoid_: Blog, front end, live site\n\n**Draft**:\nA Recap's or Page's status while it is still being written. Every Recap and Page starts as a Draft, and Drafts never leave the database.\n\n**Submitted**:\nA Recap's status once its Editor says it is finished and ready for an Admin to review. Nobody but an Admin can change it from here.\n_Avoid_: Pending, in review\n\n**Published**:\nA Recap's or Page's status once an Admin has approved it for the public site. It is not visible to readers until the next Deploy.\n\n**Submit**:\nAn Editor moving their own Recap from Draft to Submitted.\n\n**Send back**:\nAn Admin returning a Submitted Recap to Draft so its Editor can revise it.\n_Avoid_: Reject\n\n**Publish / Unpublish**:\nMoving a Recap or Page to Published, or from Published back to Draft. Only Admins Publish or Unpublish.\n_Avoid_: using \"publish\" for rebuilding the site\n\n**Deploy**:\nRebuilding the Public site from the Trips, Published Recaps, and Published Pages, and pushing it live. Only Admins deploy. A Deploy is two commands: `cms publish` renders the Public site into `site/`, and `cms deploy` pushes it live. Despite its name, `cms publish` does not Publish anything.\n_Avoid_: Publish (for this action), build, push\n\n**Backup**:\nA dated archive of the database and uploaded Images, kept somewhere private outside the repository. It is the only copy of Drafts and Recap sources if the Console laptop is lost. Only Admins make Backups.\n\n## Operations\n\n**Console laptop**:\nThe single machine (the President's) that runs the admin console and holds the one real database. Admins work on it, and Editors log in on it during the Sunday club meetings.\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly transfer to new officers: outgoing Admins create the incoming Admins' Accounts, incoming Admins Deactivate the outgoing ones, and the Console laptop or latest Backup moves with them.\n\n## People\n\n**Account**:\nOne person's login to the admin console, carrying their name, class year, and role (Admin or Editor). An Account is either active or Deactivated.\n_Avoid_: User (in prose), profile, login\n\n**Deactivate**:\nAn Admin switching off an Account so it can no longer log in. Its Recaps, Pages, and Bylines stay as they are. The last active Admin can never be Deactivated.\n_Avoid_: Delete, remove, ban\n\n**Admin**:\nThe club's President or Vice President. Admins can do everything an Editor can, and also Publish and Unpublish, Send back, create, edit, and delete Trips, create, edit, and delete Pages, create Accounts, change an Account's role, Deactivate Accounts, Deploy, and make Backups. They can edit or delete any Recap and enter one on a Contributor's behalf.\n_Avoid_: Officer (in the system), superuser\n\n**Editor**:\nA club member with their own Account who writes their own Recaps as Drafts, adds Images with alt text to them, and Submits them. An Editor can edit or delete their own Recap only while it is a Draft. The President and VP decide which members become Editors, and an Admin creates the Account. An Editor cannot Publish or Unpublish, create Trips, create or edit Pages, manage Accounts, Deploy, make Backups, or edit another person's Recap.\n_Avoid_: Author, writer, contributor (for this role)\n\n**Contributor**:\nA member whose writing an Admin enters for them, for example because they missed a Sunday meeting and emailed it in. A Contributor has no Account of their own.\n_Avoid_: Editor (for this role), author, writer\nT03\napp/\ndev/\ndocs/\nnotes/\nscripts/\ntemplates/\ntests/\ntranscripts/\nAGENTS.md  1.2K\nCLAUDE.md  3.6K\nCONTEXT.md  6.4K\nREADME.md  2.3K\nSECURITY-CHECKLIST.md  1.5K\ncms.db  12.0K\npyproject.toml  933B\nuv.lock  184.4K","is_error":false},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/tdd\n\n# Test-Driven Development\n\nTDD is the red → green loop. This skill is the reference that makes that loop produce tests worth keeping: what a good test is, where tests go, the anti-patterns, and the rules of the loop. Every section applies on every cycle: consult them before and during the loop, not after.\n\nWhen exploring the codebase, read `CONTEXT.md` (if it exists) so test names and interface vocabulary match the project's domain language, and respect ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n## What a good test is\n\nTests verify behavior through public interfaces, not implementation details. Code can change entirely; tests shouldn't. A good test reads like a specification: \"user can checkout with valid cart\" tells you exactly what capability exists, and it survives refactors because it doesn't care about internal structure.\n\nSee [tests.md](tests.md) for examples and [mocking.md](mocking.md) for mocking guidelines.\n\n## Seams: where tests go\n\nA **seam** is the public boundary you test at: the interface where you observe behavior without reaching inside. Tests live at seams, never against internals.\n\n**Test only at pre-agreed seams.** Before writing any test, write down the seams under test and confirm them with the user. No test is written at an unconfirmed seam. You can't test everything, so agreeing the seams up front is how testing effort lands on the critical paths and complex logic instead of every edge case.\n\nAsk: \"What's the public interface, and which seams should we test?\"\n\nWhen the shape of that interface is itself in question (how deep the module is, where the seam belongs, what the interface should expose), call the Skill tool with \"codebase-design\" for the vocabulary. It is the shared source of the module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage and locality terms, and it is a reference to consult, not a session to run.\n\n## Anti-patterns\n\n- **Implementation-coupled**: mocks internal collaborators, tests private methods, or verifies through a side channel (querying the database instead of using the interface). The tell: the test breaks when you refactor but behavior hasn't changed.\n- **Tautological**: the assertion recomputes the expected value the way the code does (`expect(add(a, b)).toBe(a + b)`, a snapshot derived by hand the same way, a constant asserted equal to itself), so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code. Expected values must come from an independent source of truth: a known-good literal, a worked example, the spec.\n- **Horizontal slicing**: writing all tests first, then all implementation. Bulk tests verify _imagined_ behavior: you test the _shape_ of things rather than user-facing behavior, the tests go insensitive to real changes, and you commit to test structure before understanding the implementation. Work in **vertical slices** instead: one test → one implementation → repeat, each test a **tracer bullet** that responds to what the last cycle taught you.\n\n## Rules of the loop\n\n- **Red before green.** Write the failing test first, then only enough code to pass it. Don't anticipate future tests or add speculative features.\n- **One slice at a time.** One seam, one test, one minimal implementation per cycle.\n- **Refactoring is not part of the loop.** It belongs to the review stage (see the `code-review` skill), not the red → green implementation cycle.\n"}]}}

Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. A ticket is unblocked when every blocker is closed.\n- **Frontier query**: list the map's open children (`gh issue list --state open`, scoped to the map's sub-issues / task list), drop any with an open blocker (`issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by > 0`, or an open issue in the `Blocked by` line) or an assignee; first in map order wins.\n- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> --add-assignee @me`, the session's first write.\n- **Resolve**: `gh issue comment <n> --body \"<answer>\"`, then `gh issue close <n>`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far.\nroutes/\nadmin/\npublic/\n__init__.py  216B\naccounts.py  4.2K\ncli.py  1.9K\ndb.py  1.1K\nmain.py  1.5K\npolicy.py  819B\npublish.py  1.5K\nsecurity.py  2.0K\nseed.py  597B\nsettings.py  915B\ntemplating.py  303B\nADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md  1.4K\nADR-002-stack.md  1.1K\nADR-003-editors-at-sunday-meetings.md  2.1K\nbase.html  523B\nconftest.py  2.3K\ntest_ctx_guard.py  3.2K\ntest_t00.py  950B\ntest_t01.py  6.3K\ntest_t02.py  15.4K\ntest_usage_report.py  2.6K\n... A Trip has a conference name, host city, start date, end date, Summary and Slug. The Slug is suggested from the start year and city, such as `2026-chicago`, and can be edited. It must be unique among Trips. Deleting a Trip is refused while it still has Recaps. Editors are refused on every Trip write route.\n\n**Recap Drafts with ownership.** An Editor creates a Recap by picking its Trip from a list and entering a title, a Slug (suggested from the title) and a Markdown Body. Every Recap starts as a Draft. The Editor's Byline (name and class year) is copied from their Account when the Recap is created. An Admin entering a Contributor's emailed writing types the Contributor's name and class year as the Byline instead. Each Recap records its Owner and when it was created and last edited. A Recap's Slug must be unique within its Trip. Saving with an empty Body is refused. Editors may view, edit and delete only Drafts they Own. Admins may edit or delete any Recap, and can edit the Byline.\n\nSettled: the Byline is copied at creation, so renaming or Deactivating an Account later doesn't rewrite it. Editors see only their own Recaps.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n\n- [ ] An Admin can create, edit, list and delete Trips. All five fields and the Slug are required.\n- [ ] The Trip Slug is suggested from the year and city, can be edited, and a duplicate is refused with a clear error.\n- [ ] Deleting a Trip that has any Recap is refused, and the Trip remains.\n- [ ] An Editor can create a Recap on an existing Trip, chosen from a list, and the Recap starts as a Draft.\n- [ ] The Recap Slug is suggested from the title. A Slug that clashes within the same Trip is refused with a clear error, and the same Slug on a different Trip is allowed.\n- [ ] Saving a Recap with an empty or whitespace-only Body is refused.\n- [ ] An Editor's Byline is filled in from their Account. An Admin can create a Recap with a typed Contributor Byline, and Owner is still set to the Admin.\n- [ ] Renaming the Owner's Account later doesn't change existing Bylines.\n- [ ] Owner, created and edited timestamps are recorded and shown in the editor.\n- [ ] An Editor can edit and delete their own Draft.\n- [ ] An Editor's requests to view, edit or delete another person's Recap are refused, and that Recap is unchanged.\n- [ ] An Admin can edit or delete any Recap, including its Byline.\n- [ ] The Trip write routes are added to the table-driven Editor test.\n- [ ] Every form carries a CSRF token.\n\n## Blocked by\n\n- #2 (T01)\n\n(eval):1: =====SPEC not found","serverClassifierContext":{"request":"22e6b5d9-9405-4b03-928c-336dd06e7f40","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"main","default_branch":null,"status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":1,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":9},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"andrew-vera26/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"macos"}},"sandboxed":false,"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"d4b857be-7a1b-40f6-964a-31a83c70eaf1","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"3548b646-8d3a-4de6-a0ab-d101cad45aeb","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c90d8a8e-bdff-479f-a559-176fea855e44","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","content":"Exit code 1\nVocabulary follows `CONTEXT.md`. Decisions behind it: ADR-001 (local admin console, static Public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Editors write at the Sunday meetings; only Admins Publish).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe Kenyon Model UN club has no website. Trip recaps go on Instagram, where they sink in the feed, so nobody in the Kenyon community can look back at a past Trip. The President and Vice President want a place where members' Recaps of each Trip (where the team went, how the competition went, what they explored and ate) are published with photos and stay findable. Members need to be able to write their own Recaps. The officers must stay in control of what reaches readers, and no member can ever change another member's work or touch accounts.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the **Console laptop**. Admins and Editors log in to it. Editors write their own Recaps at the Sunday club meetings and Submit them. Admins review, edit, Send back, or Publish them. Admins also manage Trips, Pages, and Accounts, and enter Recaps for Contributors who email their writing in.\n- A static **Public site** that an Admin Deploys from the terminal. It lists Trips newest first. Each Trip page shows its Summary and then its Published Recaps. Admin-written Pages, such as \"About the club\", form the Navigation bar. A footer link sends readers to Instagram for discussion. Only Published content reaches the Public site, and all of it is sanitized.\n\nAn Admin can also take a dated Backup of the database and Images with `cms backup`, so losing the laptop doesn't lose the club's writing.\n\n## User Stories\n\n**Login and Accounts**\n\n1. As an Admin, I want to log in with my email and password, so that only I can use Admin powers on the Console laptop.\n2. As an Editor, I want to log in with my own Account at the Sunday meeting, so that my Recaps are mine and nobody else's.\n3. As any logged-in person, I want to sign out, so that the next member at the laptop can't act as me.\n4. As an anonymous visitor to the console, I want to be redirected to the login page from every console page, so that nothing in the console is reachable without an Account.\n5. As an Admin, I want passwords stored only as argon2 hashes, so that a copied database doesn't reveal anyone's password.\n6. As a person who typed a wrong password, I want a generic \"email or password is incorrect\" message, so that the login page doesn't reveal which emails have Accounts.\n7. As an Admin, I want a Deactivated Account to be unable to log in, and any session it already has to stop working, so that a member who leaves the club loses access immediately.\n\n**Roles and permissions**\n\n8. As an Admin, I want Editors to get a 403 or a redirect on every Admin-only page and action, so that the Editor role is genuinely limited.\n9. As an Editor, I want to create Recaps, edit and delete my own Drafts, add Images to them, and Submit them, so that I can contribute without waiting on an officer.\n10. As an Admin, I want an Editor to be unable to Publish or Unpublish anything, so that Published always means an Admin approved it.\n11. As an Editor, I want to be refused when I try to view, edit, Submit, or delete another person's Recap, so that nobody can tamper with my writing.\n12. As an Editor, I want my Recap locked against my own edits once it is Submitted or Published, so that what an Admin reviewed doesn't change underneath them.\n13. As an Admin, I want to do everything an Editor can, and also edit or delete any Recap, so that I can fix typos and take down anything inappropriate.\n\n**Trips**\n\n14. As an Admin, I want to create a Trip with a conference name, host city, start date, end date, and Summary, so that Recaps have something to belong to.\n15. As an Admin, I want the Trip's Slug suggested from its year and city (such as `2026-chicago`) and editable, so that addresses are readable.\n16. As an Admin, I want to edit any Trip, so that I can correct its Summary or dates later.\n17. As an Admin, I want deleting a Trip refused while it still has Recaps, so that Recaps are never lost along with their Trip.\n18. As an Editor, I want to pick the Trip my Recap is about from a list, so that I can't misspell or invent a Trip.\n\n**Recaps**\n\n19. As an Editor, I want to write a Recap with a title, a Slug, and a Markdown Body, so that I can tell my story with basic formatting.\n20. As an Editor, I want the Slug suggested from the title, so that I don't have to think about URLs.\n21. As an Admin, I want a Recap's Slug to be unique within its Trip, with a clear error on a clash, so that two Recaps never share an address.\n22. As an Editor, I want my Byline (name and class year) filled in from my Account, so that I'm credited correctly without typing it.\n23. As an Admin entering a Contributor's emailed Recap, I want to type their name and class year as the Byline, so that the Contributor is credited and not me.\n24. As an Admin, I want every Recap to record i\n\n... [4579 characters truncated] ...\n\nsfers cleanly each year.\n\n**Public site and Deploy**\n\n55. As a Kenyon reader, I want the home page to list Trips newest first, so that I see the latest Trip immediately and can scroll back to older ones.\n56. As a reader, I want each Trip's page to show its Summary and then its Published Recaps in the order they were Published, with their Bylines, so that I get the overview and then each member's story.\n57. As a reader, I want a Trip to appear only once it has at least one Published Recap, so that I never land on an empty Trip.\n58. As a reader, I want a Navigation bar with Home first, then the Published Pages in the order the Admins set, so that \"About the club\" is always one click away.\n59. As a reader, I want a footer link to the club's Instagram for discussion, so that I can react to a Recap even though the site has no comments.\n60. As an Admin, I want `cms publish` to write only Published Recaps and Pages, and only Trips that have a Published Recap, into `site/`, so that Drafts and Submitted Recaps never leak.\n61. As an Admin, I want every Body sanitized when it is rendered, with scripts and raw HTML stripped and external links and external images removed, so that nothing harmful or off-site reaches readers.\n62. As an Admin, I want every link and image in `site/` to be a relative path, so that the site works from the GitHub Pages subfolder.\n63. As an Admin, I want only the Images of Published Recaps copied into `site/`, so that photos from Drafts never become public.\n64. As an Admin, I want `cms deploy` to push `site/` live, so that a Deploy is `cms publish` followed by `cms deploy`.\n\n**Backup and seed data**\n\n65. As an Admin, I want `cms backup` to write one dated archive containing the database and all uploaded Images to a folder I choose outside the repository, so that I can keep a private copy on the club's Drive.\n66. As an Admin, I want `cms backup` to refuse to write inside the repository, so that a Backup can never be committed by accident.\n67. As a grader, I want the seed script to create one Admin and one Editor (passwords from the environment), a Trip, Recaps in each status, and a Draft and a Published Page, so that I can try every capability on a fresh clone.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n**Storage.** SQLite through the standard library, at the existing database path setting. Trip recaps go on Instagram, where they sink in the feed, so nobody in the Kenyon community can look back at a past Trip. The President and Vice President want a place where members' Recaps of each Trip (where the team went, how the competition went, what they explored and ate) are published with photos and stay findable. Members need to be able to write their own Recaps. The officers must stay in control of what reaches readers, and no member can ever change another member's work or touch accounts.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS with two halves:\n\n- An **admin console** that runs only on the **Console laptop**. Admins and Editors log in to it. Editors write their own Recaps at the Sunday club meetings and Submit them. Admins review, edit, Send back, or Publish them. Admins also manage Trips, Pages, and Accounts, and enter Recaps for Contributors who email their writing in.\n- A static **Public site** that an Admin Deploys from the terminal. Add routes in their own modules under app/routes/ and\ninclude them here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console\nfrom app.security import csrf_protect\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_DEV_DEFAULT:\n        log.warning(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY is not set: sessions are signed with the \"\n                    \"public development key. Development use only.\")\n    db.init_db()\n    # csrf_protect runs on every route, so no state-changing route can skip it.\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", dependencies=[Depends(csrf_protect)])\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"lax\",\n                       https_only=False)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The permission policy: can this Account do this action to this object?\n\nEvery route asks `can` (through `security.require`); routes never check roles\nthemselves. Unknown actions are denied. Add an action here when a ticket adds a\ncapability. Rules that depend on the object (an Editor's own Draft) take the\n`obj` argument.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nADMIN = \"admin\"\nEDITOR = \"editor\"\n\n# action -> roles allowed to do it\nROLE_RULES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {\n    \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n}\n\n\ndef can(account: Account | None, action: str, obj: object | None = None) -> bool:\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        return False\n    return account.role in ROLE_RULES.get(action, frozenset())\n\"\"\"SQLite access. The database path is read from settings on every call.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS account (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    name          TEXT NOT NULL,\n    class_year    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open a connection; commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        yield conn\n        conn.commit()\n    except BaseException:\n        conn.rollback()\n        raise\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n\"\"\"Sessions, CSRF and the route guard.\n\nThe session is a signed cookie (Starlette's SessionMiddleware, itsdangerous\nunderneath) holding the Account id and a CSRF token. The Account itself is\nreread from the database on every request.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport secrets\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, HTTPException, Request\n\nfrom app import accounts, policy\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nSAFE_METHODS = {\"GET\", \"HEAD\", \"OPTIONS\"}\nLOGIN_URL = \"/login\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use.\"\"\"\n    token = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not token:\n        token = request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return token\n\n\nasync def csrf_protect(request: Request) -> None:\n    \"\"\"App-wide dependency: refuse any state-changing request without the token.\"\"\"\n    if request.method in SAFE_METHODS:\n        return\n    form = await request.form()\n    sent = form.get(\"csrf_token\")\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\")\n    if not (isinstance(sent, str) and expected\n            and secrets.compare_digest(sent, expected)):\n        raise HTTPException(403, \"Missing or invalid CSRF token\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account | None:\n    \"\"\"Reread the signed-in Account; a Deactivated one counts as signed out.\"\"\"\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = accounts.get(account_id) if account_id else None\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.pop(\"account_id\", None)\n        return None\n    return account\n\n\ndef require(action: str) -> Callable[..., Account]:\n    \"\"\"Route dependency: logged out -> login page, not allowed -> 403.\"\"\"\n\n    def guard(account: Account | None = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n        if account is None:\n            raise HTTPException(303, headers={\"Location\": LOGIN_URL})\n        if not policy.can(account, action):\n            raise HTTPException(403, \"You do not have permission to do that\")\n        return account\n\n    return guard\n\"\"\"The shared Jinja environment for the console.\"\"\"\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.security import csrf_token\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token  # {{ csrf_token(request) }}\n\"\"\"Demo Accounts, shared by scripts/seed_demo.py and the test fixtures.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app import accounts, db\n\nADMIN_EMAIL = \"admin@example.test\"\nEDITOR_EMAIL = \"editor@example.test\"\n\n\ndef seed_accounts(admin_password: str, editor_password: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the demo Admin and Editor. {"parentUuid":"1b009338-ecf0-4bb8-b957-6c67378cb5d7","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c90d8a8e-bdff-479f-a559-176fea855e44","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019XvHjjo62aAzqLYdTaVmx8","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"T01: log in, sign out, CSRF and the permission policy.\"\"\"\nimport logging\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom app import accounts, db\nfrom tests.conftest import DEMO_USERS, csrf_from, log_in\n\nGENERIC = \"email or password is incorrect\"\n\n# Every Admin-only route and action, as (method, path). Each later ticket adds\n# its own rows; an Editor must get a 403 (or a redirect) on all of them.\nADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES: list[tuple[str, str]] = [\n    # T02: Account management\n    (\"GET\", \"/admin/accounts\"),\n    (\"GET\", \"/admin/accounts/new\"),\n    (\"POST\", \"/admin/accounts\"),\n    (\"POST\", \"/admin/accounts/1/role\"),\n    (\"POST\", \"/admin/accounts/1/deactivate\"),\n    (\"POST\", \"/admin/accounts/1/password\"),\n]\n\n\n@pytest.mark.parametrize(\"method,path\", ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES)\ndef test_editor_on_admin_only_routes(client_as, method, path):\n    c = client_as(\"editor\")\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))\n    r = c.request(method, path, data={\"csrf_token\": token},\n                  follow_redirects=False)\n    assert r.status_code in (302, 303, 403)\n\n\n# ---- login / logout -------------------------------------------------------\n\n\"\"\"T02: Account management (Admin only).\"\"\"\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import accounts, db\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom tests.conftest import DEMO_USERS, csrf_from, log_in\n\nGENERIC = \"email or password is incorrect\"\nLIST = \"/admin/accounts\"\nNEW_FORM = \"/admin/accounts/new\"\n\nNEW_ACCOUNT = {\"email\": \"new.editor@example.test\", \"name\": \"New Editor\",\n               \"class_year\": \"2029\", \"role\": \"editor\",\n               \"password\": \"new-editor-pw\"}\n\n\n# ---- helpers --------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef account_id(email):\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        row = conn.execute(\"SELECT id FROM account WHERE email = ?\",\n                           (email,)).fetchone()\n    return row[\"id\"] if row else None\n\n\ndef account_count():\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(\"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM account\").fetchone()[0]\n\n\ndef post(c, path, **data):\n    \"\"\"POST a form with a valid CSRF token taken from the Accounts list.\"\"\"\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(LIST))\n    return c.post(path, data={\"csrf_token\": token, **data},\n                  follow_redirects=False)\n\n\ndef create(c, **overrides):\n    return post(c, LIST, **{**NEW_ACCOUNT, **overrides})\n\n\ndef signed_in(email, password):\n    \"\"\"A fresh client signed in as this Account; its login response too.\"\"\"\n    c = TestClient(create_app())\n    return c, log_in(c, email, password)\n\n\ndef make_second_admin():\n    accounts.create_account(\"second.admin@example.test\", \"Second Admin\", 2026,\n app.main import create_app\n\nTRIPS = \"/admin/trips\"\nRECAPS = \"/admin/recaps\"\n\nCHICAGO = {\"conference\": \"Chicago International MUN\", \"city\": \"Chicago\",\n           \"start_date\": \"2026-03-05\", \"end_date\": \"2026-03-08\",\n           \"summary\": \"Four days of committee work in Chicago.\",\n           \"slug\": \"2026-chicago\"}\nBOSTON = {\"conference\": \"Boston \"2026-boston\"}\n\nBODY = \"We **landed** at O'Hare and the food crawl began.\"\n\n\n# ---- helpers --------------------------------------------------------------\n\ndef post(c, path, **data):\n    \"\"\"POST a form with a valid CSRF token taken from the console home.\"\"\"\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))\n    return c.post(path, data={\"csrf_token\": token, **data},\n recap_form(trip_id, **overrides):\n    return {\"trip_id\": str(trip_id), \"title\": \"Chicago food crawl\",\n            \"slug\": \"chicago-food-crawl\", \"body\": BODY, **overrides}\n\n\ndef make_recap(c, trip_id, **overrides):\n    r = post(c, RECAPS, **recap_form(trip_id, **overrides))\n    assert r.status_code == 303, r.text\n    slug = recap_form(trip_id, **overrides)[\"slug\"]\n \"\"\"POST a form with a valid CSRF token taken from the console home.\"\"\"\n    token = csrf_from(c.get(\"/admin\"))\n    return c.post(path, data={\"csrf_token\": token, **data},\n  def attempt(email, password):\n        r = log_in(client, email, password)\n        assert r.status_code == 401\n        return r.text\n\n    wrong_pw = attempt(DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], log_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"], \"wrong-password-xyz\")\n        log_in(client, DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"email\"],\n               DEMO_USERS[\"admin\"][\"password\"])\n    with The database path is read from settings on every call.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom typing import Iterator\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS account (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    name          TEXT NOT NULL,\n    class_year    INTEGER NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,\n    created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect() -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open a connection; commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\"\"\"\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(settings.DATABASE_PATH)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    try:\n        yield conn\n        conn.commit()\n    except BaseException:\n        conn.rollback()\n        raise\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init_db() -> None:\n    with connect() as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":18,"oldLines":6,"newStart":18,"newLines":18,"lines":["     active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,","     created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))"," );","+","+CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trip (","+    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,","+    conference TEXT NOT NULL,","+    city       TEXT NOT NULL,","+    start_date TEXT NOT NULL,","+    end_date   TEXT NOT NULL,","+    summary    TEXT NOT NULL,","+    slug       TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,","+    created_at TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now')),","+    edited_at  TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now'))","+);"," \"\"\""," "," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"7f61d8c5-c94a-4c78-ae95-a80ec3ffffc6","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

Unknown actions are denied. Add an action here when a ticket adds a\ncapability. Rules that depend on the object (an Editor's own Draft) take the\n`obj` argument.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nADMIN = \"admin\"\nEDITOR = \"editor\"\n\n# action -> roles allowed to do it\nROLE_RULES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {\n    \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n}\n\n\ndef can(account: Account | None, action: str, obj: object | None = None) -> bool:\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        return False\n    return account.role in ROLE_RULES.get(action, frozenset())\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":16,"oldLines":6,"newStart":16,"newLines":7,"lines":[" ROLE_RULES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {","     \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),","     \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),","+    \"trips.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),"," }"," "," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"454c3954-65ba-47dc-ba11-32e471680a9d","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

Admins manage them.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\n\nfrom app import db\n\nFIELDS = (\"conference\", \"city\", \"start_date\", \"end_date\", \"summary\", \"slug\")\n\n\ndef create_trip(values: dict[str, str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Insert a Trip from the six form fields; return its id.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        cur = conn.execute(\n            f\"INSERT INTO trip ({', '.join(FIELDS)}) \"\n            f\"VALUES ({', '.join('?' for _ in FIELDS)})\",\n            [values[f] for f in FIELDS])\n        return cur.lastrowid\n\n\ndef list_trips() -> list[sqlite3.Row]:\n    \"\"\"All Trips, newest start date first.\"\"\"\n    with db.connect() as conn:\n        return conn.execute(\n            \"SELECT * FROM trip ORDER BY start_date DESC, id DESC\").fetchall()\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1835816c-25b2-45f3-b7b9-a23c4ec8cd11","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

Add routes in their own modules under app/routes/ and\ninclude them here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console\nfrom app.security import csrf_protect\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_DEV_DEFAULT:\n        log.warning(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY is not set: sessions are signed with the \"\n                    \"public development key. Development use only.\")\n    db.init_db()\n    # csrf_protect runs on every route, so no state-changing route can skip it.\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", dependencies=[Depends(csrf_protect)])\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"lax\",\n                       https_only=False)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":12,"oldLines":7,"newStart":12,"newLines":7,"lines":[" from starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware"," "," from app import db, settings","-from app.routes import accounts, auth, console","+from app.routes import accounts, auth, console, trips"," from app.security import csrf_protect"," from app.templating import templates"," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"997f67f3-87dd-4d93-b5a5-026529baad75","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

Add routes in their own modules under app/routes/ and\ninclude them here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, trips\nfrom app.security import csrf_protect\nfrom app.templating import templates\n\n\nlog = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    if settings.SECRET_KEY_IS_DEV_DEFAULT:\n        log.warning(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY is not set: sessions are signed with the \"\n                    \"public development key. Development use only.\")\n    db.init_db()\n    # csrf_protect runs on every route, so no state-changing route can skip it.\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\", dependencies=[Depends(csrf_protect)])\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", same_site=\"lax\",\n                       https_only=False)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":34,"oldLines":6,"newStart":34,"newLines":7,"lines":["     app.include_router(auth.router)","     app.include_router(console.router)","     app.include_router(accounts.router)","+    app.include_router(trips.router)"," ","     @app.get(\"/\")","     def public_home(request: Request):"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"f8a55369-bae8-495c-a80b-806f01211255","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

The suggestion needs a small `slugify` that the Recap form will reuse, and the new-Trip route needs to read the query params."},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_011eM4hMRkDUMEVDVTYockm7","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/slugs.py","content":"\"\"\"Suggested Slugs. A suggestion is only a starting point; the Admin or Editor\ncan edit it, and uniqueness is checked when the form is saved.\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nimport unicodedata\n\n\ndef slugify(text: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"URL-safe form of text: lowercase ASCII letters and digits, joined by\n    single hyphens.\"\"\"\n    ascii_text = (unicodedata.normalize(\"NFKD\", text)\n                  .encode(\"ascii\", \"ignore\").decode())\n    return re.sub(r\"[^a-z0-9]+\", \"-\", ascii_text.lower()).strip(\"-\")\n\n\ndef suggest_trip_slug(start_date: str, city: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Start year plus city, such as 2026-chicago; empty until both are known.\"\"\"\n    year, city_slug = start_date.strip()[:4], slugify(city)\n    return f\"{year}-{city_slug}\" if year.isdigit() and city_slug else \"\"\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01MbkomLAPriRUKcR2cUzokx","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/trips.py","old_string":"@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef new_trip(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(manage)):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/trip_form.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"New Trip\", \"account\": account, \"values\": {}, \"error\": None})","new_string":"@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef new_trip(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(manage),\n             start_date: str = \"\", city: str = \"\"):\n    values = {\"start_date\": start_date, \"city\": city,\n              \"slug\": slugs.suggest_trip_slug(start_date, city)}\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/trip_form.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"New Trip\", \"account\": account, \"values\": values,\n         \"error\": None})"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01X8k2MjC5m2Tw4sb7MjdFso","name":"Edit","input":{"file_path":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/routes/trips.py","old_string":"from app import trips\n","new_string":"from app import slugs, trips\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}},{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_016NBPjRiaKLJ3b8qzZuEkM9","name":"Bash","input":{"command":"uv run pytest tests/test_t03.py -q --tb=short -k \"slug_is_suggested_from_year\" 2>&1 | tail -6; templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/trip_form.html\",\n        {\"title\": title, \"account\": account, \"values\": values,\n         \"action\": action, \"error\": error}, status_code=status_code)\n\n\ndef _save(request: Request, account: Account, values: dict[str, str],\n          save: Callable[[dict[str, str]], object], action: str, title: str):\n    \"\"\"Validate and save; re-show the form with a 400 and a message if refused.\"\"\"\n    error = None\n    if not all(values.values()):\n        error = \"Every field is required.\"\n    else:\n        try:\n            save(values)\n        except trips.SlugTaken:\n            error = SLUG_TAKEN_ERROR\n    if error:\n        return _form(request, account, values, action, title, error, 400)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/trips\", status_code=303)\n\n\ndef _trip_or_404(trip_id: int):\n    trip = trips.get_trip(trip_id)\n    if trip is None:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"No such Trip\")\n    return trip\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef list_trips(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(manage)):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/trips.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Trips\", \"account\": account, \"trips\": trips.list_trips()})\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef new_trip(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(manage),\n             start_date: str = \"\", city: str = \"\"):\n    values = {\"start_date\": start_date, \"city\": city,\n              \"slug\": slugs.suggest_trip_slug(start_date, city)}\n    return _form(request, account, values, \"/admin/trips\", \"New Trip\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef create_trip(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(manage),\n                conference: str = Form(\"\"), city: str = conference.strip(), \"city\": city.strip(),\n              \"start_date\": start_date.strip(), \"end_date\": end_date.strip(),\n              \"summary\": summary.strip(), \"slug\": slug.strip()}\n    return _save(request, account, values, trips.create_trip,\n                 \"/admin/trips\", \"New Trip\")\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{trip_id}\")\ndef edit_trip_form(trip_id: int, request: Request,\n                   account: Account = Depends(manage)):\n    return _form(request, account, _trip_or_404(trip_id),\n                 f\"/admin/trips/{trip_id}\", \"Edit Trip\")\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{trip_id}\")\ndef edit_trip(trip_id: int, request: Request,\n              account: Account = Depends(manage),\n              conference: str = Form(\"\"), city: str = Form(\"\"),\n              start_date: str = Form(\"\"), end_date: str = Form(\"\"),\n              summary: str = Form(\"\"), slug: str = Form(\"\")):\n    _trip_or_404(trip_id)\n    values = Unknown actions are denied. Add an action here when a ticket adds a\ncapability. Rules that depend on the object (an Editor's own Draft) take the\n`obj` argument.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\nADMIN = \"admin\"\nEDITOR = \"editor\"\n\n# action -> roles allowed to do it\nROLE_RULES: dict[str, frozenset[str]] = {\n    \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),\n    \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n    \"trips.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),\n}\n\n\ndef can(account: Account | None, action: str, obj: object | None = None) -> bool:\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        return False\n    return account.role in ROLE_RULES.get(action, frozenset())\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":17,"oldLines":6,"newStart":17,"newLines":7,"lines":["     \"console.view\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),","     \"accounts.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),","     \"trips.manage\": frozenset({ADMIN}),","+    \"recaps.create\": frozenset({ADMIN, EDITOR}),"," }"," "," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"0f933275-b52b-45ec-b5fd-53a4fff8ea12","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"mode"},"session_id":"9dbdcd61-9843-4f89-8b21-3507a429536c","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/andrewv/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","version":"2.1.309","gitBranch":"main"}

An Admin types the Contributor's name and class year.\n    \"\"\"\n    if account.role != policy.ADMIN:\n        return account.name, account.class_year\n    name, class_year = name.strip(), class_year.strip()\n    if not name or not CLASS_YEAR.fullmatch(class_year) \\\n            or int(class_year) not in CLASS_YEAR_RANGE:\n        return None\n    return name, int(class_year)\n\n\n@router.post(\"\")\ndef create_recap(request: Request,\n                 account: Account = Depends(require(\"recaps.create\")),\n                 trip_id: int = Form(...), title: str = Form(\"\"),\n                 slug: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n                 byline_name: str = Form(\"\"),\n                 byline_class_year: str = Form(\"\")):\n    byline = _byline(account, byline_name, byline_class_year)\n    if byline is None:\n        values = {\"trip_id\": trip_id, \"title\": title, \"slug\": slug,\n                  \"body\": body, \"byline_name\": byline_name,\n                  \"byline_class_year\": byline_class_year}\n        return _form(request, account, values, \"/admin/recaps\", \"New Recap\",\n                     BYLINE_ERROR, 400)\n    recaps.create_recap(trip_id, account.id, title.strip(), slug.strip(), body,\n                        *byline)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/recaps\", status_code=303)\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":20,"newStart":1,"newLines":61,"lines":[" \"\"\"Recap Drafts: Editors write their own; The Owner,\n    status and created time never change here. Raises SlugTaken on a clash.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            conn.execute(\n                \"UPDATE recap SET trip_id = ?, title = ?, slug = ?, body = ?, \"\n                \"byline_name = ?, byline_class_year = ?, \"\n                \"edited_at = strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ', 'now') \"\n                \"WHERE id = ?\",\n                (trip_id, title, slug, body, byline_name, byline_class_year,\n                 recap_id))\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n        raise SlugTaken(slug) from exc\n\n\ndef create_recap(trip_id: int, owner_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str,\n                 byline_name: str, byline_class_year: int) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Insert a Draft Recap; return its id. The Body is stored as written.\n\n    Raises SlugTaken if the Trip already has a Recap with this Slug. The\n    UNIQUE (trip_id, slug) constraint decides, so two simultaneous saves\n    cannot both win.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with db.connect() as conn:\n            cur = conn.execute(\n                \"INSERT INTO recap (trip_id, owner_id, title, slug, body, \"\n                \"byline_name, byline_class_year) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)\",\n                (trip_id, owner_id, title, slug, body, byline_name,\n                 byline_class_year))\n            return cur.lastrowid\n    except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:\n        raise SlugTaken(slug) from exc\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":36,"oldLines":6,"newStart":36,"newLines":11,"lines":["         raise SlugTaken(slug) from exc"," "," ","+def delete_recap(recap_id: int) -> None:","+    with db.connect() as conn:","+        conn.execute(\"DELETE FROM recap WHERE id = ?\", (recap_id,))","+","+"," def create_recap(trip_id: int, owner_id: int, title: str, slug: str, body: str,","                  byline_name: str, byline_class_year: int) -> int:","     \"\"\"Insert a Draft Recap; return its id. Choose a different one.\")\n\n\ndef _form(request: Request, account: Account, values: dict, action: str,\n          title: str, error: str | None = None, status_code: int = 200,\n          recap=None):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/recap_form.html\",\n        {\"title\": title, \"account\": account, \"values\": values,\n         \"action\": action, \"trips\": trips.list_trips(), \"error\": error,\n         \"recap\": recap}, status_code=status_code)\n\n\ndef _typed_byline(name: str, class_year: str):\n    \"\"\"(name, class year) from what an Admin typed, or None if either part is\n    missing or the year is not a four-digit year.\"\"\"\n    name, class_year = name.strip(), class_year.strip()\n    if not name or not CLASS_YEAR.fullmatch(class_year) \\\n            or int(class_year) not in CLASS_YEAR_RANGE:\n        return None\n    return name, int(class_year)\n\n\ndef _allowed_recap(recap_id: int, account: Account, action: str):\n    \"\"\"The Recap, if it exists and this Account may do `action` to it.\"\"\"\n    recap = recaps.get_recap(recap_id)\n    if recap is None:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"No such Recap\")\n    if not policy.can(account, action, recap):\n        raise HTTPException(403, \"You do not have permission to do that\")\n    return recap\n\n\ndef _save(request: Request, account: Account, form: dict[str, str],\n          action: str, title: str,\n          save: Callable[[int, str, str, str, str, int], object],\n          existing=None):\n    \"\"\"Validate the form, then save with (trip_id, title, slug, body, byline\n    name, byline class year). On a refusal re-show the form with a 400.\n\n    An Editor's Byline is never read from the form: it is their Account's on\n    creation and unchanged on edit. An Admin types it.\n    \"\"\"\n    if account.role == policy.ADMIN:\n        byline = _typed_byline(form[\"byline_name\"], form[\"byline_class_year\"])\n    elif existing is not None:\n        byline = existing[\"byline_name\"], existing[\"byline_class_year\"]\n    else:\n        byline = account.name, account.class_year\n\n    trip_id = form[\"trip_id\"]\n    error = (BYLINE_ERROR if byline is None\n             else TRIP_ERROR if not trip_id.isdigit()\n             or trips.get_trip(int(trip_id)) is None\n             else TITLE_ERROR if not form[\"title\"].strip()\n             else SLUG_ERROR if not form[\"slug\"].strip()\n             else BODY_ERROR if not form[\"body\"].strip() else None)\n    if not error:\n        try:\n            save(int(trip_id), form[\"title\"].strip(), form[\"slug\"].strip(),\n                 form[\"body\"], *byline)\n        except recaps.SlugTaken:\n            error = SLUG_TAKEN_ERROR\n    if error:\n        return _form(request, account, form, action, title, error, 400,\n                     recap=existing)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/recaps\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef new_recap(request: Request,\n              account: Account = Depends(require(\"recaps.create\")),\n              title: str = \"\", trip_id: str = \"\"):\n    values = {\"trip_id\": trip_id, \"title\": title, \"slug\": slugify(title)}\n    return _form(request, account, values, \"/admin/recaps\", \"New Recap\")\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{recap_id}\")\ndef edit_recap_form(recap_id: int, request: Request,\n                    account: Account = Depends(require(\"console.view\"))):\n    recap = _allowed_recap(recap_id, account, \"recaps.view\")\n    values = {k: recap[k] for k in (\"trip_id\", \"title\", \"slug\", \"body\",\n                                    \"byline_name\", \"byline_class_year\")}\n    return _form(request, account, values, f\"/admin/recaps/{recap_id}\",\n                 \"Edit Recap\", recap=recap)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{recap_id}\")\ndef edit_recap(recap_id: int, request: Request,\n               account: Account = Depends(require(\"console.view\")),\n               trip_id: str = Form(\"\"), title: str = Form(\"\"),\n               slug: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n               byline_name: str = Form(\"\"),\n               byline_class_year: Choose a different one.\")\n\n\ndef _form(request: Request, account: Account, values: dict, action: str,\n          title: str, error: str | None = None, status_code: int = 200,\n          recap=None):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/recap_form.html\",\n        {\"title\": title, \"account\": account, \"values\": values,\n         \"action\": action, \"trips\": trips.list_trips(), \"error\": error,\n         \"recap\": recap}, status_code=status_code)\n\n\ndef _typed_byline(name: str, class_year: str):\n    \"\"\"(name, class year) from what an Admin typed, or None if either part is\n    missing or the year is not a four-digit year.\"\"\"\n    name, class_year = name.strip(), class_year.strip()\n    if not name or not CLASS_YEAR.fullmatch(class_year) \\\n            or int(class_year) not in CLASS_YEAR_RANGE:\n        return None\n    return name, int(class_year)\n\n\ndef _allowed_recap(recap_id: int, account: Account, action: str):\n    \"\"\"The Recap, if it exists and this Account may do `action` to it.\"\"\"\n    recap = recaps.get_recap(recap_id)\n    if recap is None:\n        raise HTTPException(404, \"No such Recap\")\n    if not policy.can(account, action, recap):\n        raise HTTPException(403, \"You do not have permission to do that\")\n    return recap\n\n\ndef _save(request: Request, account: Account, form: dict[str, str],\n          action: str, title: str,\n          save: Callable[[int, str, str, str, str, int], object],\n          existing=None):\n    \"\"\"Validate the form, then save with (trip_id, title, slug, body, byline\n    name, byline class year). On a refusal re-show the form with a 400.\n\n    An Editor's Byline is never read from the form: it is their Account's on\n    creation and unchanged on edit. An Admin types it.\n    \"\"\"\n    if account.role == policy.ADMIN:\n        byline = _typed_byline(form[\"byline_name\"], form[\"byline_class_year\"])\n    elif existing is not None:\n        byline = existing[\"byline_name\"], existing[\"byline_class_year\"]\n    else:\n        byline = account.name, account.class_year\n\n    trip_id = form[\"trip_id\"]\n    error = (BYLINE_ERROR if byline is None\n             else TRIP_ERROR if not trip_id.isdigit()\n             or trips.get_trip(int(trip_id)) is None\n             else TITLE_ERROR if not form[\"title\"].strip()\n             else SLUG_ERROR if not form[\"slug\"].strip()\n             else BODY_ERROR if not form[\"body\"].strip() else None)\n    if not error:\n        try:\n            save(int(trip_id), form[\"title\"].strip(), form[\"slug\"].strip(),\n                 form[\"body\"], *byline)\n        except recaps.SlugTaken:\n            error = SLUG_TAKEN_ERROR\n    if error:\n        return _form(request, account, form, action, title, error, 400,\n                     recap=existing)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/recaps\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.get(\"/new\")\ndef new_recap(request: Request,\n              account: Account = Depends(require(\"recaps.create\")),\n              title: str = \"\", trip_id: str = \"\"):\n    values = {\"trip_id\": trip_id, \"title\": title, \"slug\": slugify(title)}\n    return _form(request, account, values, \"/admin/recaps\", \"New Recap\")\n\n\n@router.get(\"/{recap_id}\")\ndef edit_recap_form(recap_id: int, request: Request,\n                    account: Account = Depends(require(\"console.view\"))):\n    recap = _allowed_recap(recap_id, account, \"recaps.view\")\n    values = {k: recap[k] for k in (\"trip_id\", \"title\", \"slug\", \"body\",\n                                    \"byline_name\", \"byline_class_year\")}\n    return _form(request, account, values, f\"/admin/recaps/{recap_id}\",\n                 \"Edit Recap\", recap=recap)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{recap_id}/delete\")\ndef delete_recap(recap_id: int,\n                 account: Account = Depends(require(\"console.view\"))):\n    _allowed_recap(recap_id, account, \"recaps.delete\")\n    recaps.delete_recap(recap_id)\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/recaps\", status_code=303)\n\n\n@router.post(\"/{recap_id}\")\ndef edit_recap(recap_id: int, request: Request,\n               account: Account = Depends(require(\"console.view\")),\n               trip_id: str = Form(\"\"), title: str = Form(\"\"),\n               slug: str = Form(\"\"), body: str = Form(\"\"),\n               byline_name: str = Form(\"\"),\n               byline_class_year: str = Form(\"\")):\n    recap = _allowed_recap(recap_id, account, _save(request, account, form, f\"/admin/recaps/{recap_id}\",\n                 \"Edit Recap\",\n                 lambda *fields: recaps.update_recap(recap_id, *fields),\n {"parentUuid":"713eeb00-0079-439b-bf14-ec79c344eaf9","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6e3abf69-554d-47cb-8f05-f0ba26780c3d","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"8214b48b-f5e4-4766-973a-d9a024f7878b","hash":"8e2977aee8c9d7d11644fe59b11605a1264195c43738d7772313a8787a784567","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"<command-message>code-review</command-message>\n<command-name>/code-review</command-name>\n"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /Users/andrewv/.claude/skills/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n"}]}}

Body is stored raw (recaps.py:182), so the sanitize-before-render rule falls to the later render ticket.\n  - SECURITY-CHECKLIST #4 and #10 are met: `require()` plus `policy.can` on the object, not link hiding. `ADMIN_ONLY_ROUTES` in test_t01 was extended.\n  \n  VOCABULARY (CONTEXT.md _Avoid_ lists), judgement calls, no hard breaks\n  - `trip_form.html:662` uses the label \"Host city\" and `trips.html` uses \"City\".
